title: Decide whether personad may make outbound network calls
description:
personad makes no outbound network connections today. Verified across the workspace: the only network reference is a ponytail note in persona-attestors/src/did_key.rs saying 'upgrade path: reqwest + did-web resolver once networking is desired'. Every attestor reads a local socket, a local file, an environment variable or a subprocess.

That is a property, not an accident, and it is worth deciding deliberately rather than losing to the first feature that wants it. A daemon that holds the user's identity keys and talks to nothing is a much smaller thing to reason about than one that fetches.

What currently wants to break it:
  did:web resolution, to verify a credential whose issuer is a domain (persona-lnaj,
    SPEC-HIA:207-210)
  OIDC token verification against an issuer's JWKS endpoint, which is the honest fix
    for persona-5s4b.30 rather than parsing an unverified payload
  SPIFFE Federation and trust bundle sync, which SPEC-HIA:884 raises as an open
    question

What it costs to allow: an outbound dependency, a cache with invalidation, behaviour that varies with the network, and an attack surface reachable by whoever controls a name that appears in local input. What it costs to refuse: did:web and did:ipfs stay unsupported, OIDC stays unverifiable without a local key, and federation needs another bootstrap.

A middle position exists and may be the right one: no network in the daemon, and a separate short-lived helper the user runs to fetch and cache what the daemon then reads locally. That keeps the daemon's posture while making the data reachable, at the cost of a second moving part.
design:
SUPERSEDED. Mark reversed this on 2026-09-14, the same day: personad MAY make outbound network connections. Implemented in the commit following 5edfbb6, which reverts it.

REASON FOR THE REVERSAL: several sources are defined by network resolution and have no local substitute. did:web IS an HTTPS fetch of a DID document -- there is no offline form. OIDC verification means fetching the issuer's JWKS. SPIFFE Federation syncs bundles between hosts. Refusing the network does not make those local, it makes them unsupported.

The refuse-and-enforce analysis read 'nothing concrete needs the network' off the code as it stands today, which mistook the current state for the intended one. The daemon connects to nothing because the online sources are not built yet, not because they were rejected.

WHAT SURVIVES: where a source can reach its data through a local daemon that already fetches, it still should -- tailscale.rs speaks the LocalAPI over /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock rather than calling the coordination server. That is an efficiency, not a boundary. And a resolved name generally arrives from local input personad does not control, so it is untrusted input.

STILL TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING (measured while implementing the now-reverted position): IPAddressDeny= does nothing in a systemd user unit -- the BPF firewall is not delegated to the user manager, so systemd accepts the setting and silently ignores it (curl got HTTP 200 through it on a cgroup v2 host). RestrictAddressFamilies= does work there, being seccomp. Recorded as memory systemd-user-unit-ipaddressdeny-is-a-noop. Relevant if anyone later wants to sandbox personad's network access by destination rather than forbid it.
close_reason:
DECIDED by Mark 2026-09-14: personad makes no outbound network connections, and the Linux user unit enforces it. Implemented in 5edfbb6 (SPEC-HIA Daemon section + systemd/personad.service).

Enforcement is RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX, NOT IPAddressDeny=any. IPAddressDeny does NOTHING in a systemd user unit -- the BPF firewall is not delegated to the user manager (it delegates only cpu/memory/pids), so systemd accepts the setting and silently ignores it. Measured on this cgroup v2 host: curl returned HTTP 200 through it. The seccomp filter was measured the same way (curl 000), and personad was run under it: starts, registers all five sources, binds the UDS, serves, shuts down clean.

Update to this bead's own framing: one of its three drivers was already dead. It cited JWKS verification as the honest fix for persona-5s4b.30, but .30 closed WITHOUT network -- SelfAssertedDomain has no OrgOidc variant, so an unverified iss cannot anchor a trust domain at all. did:web and federation remain and are both speculative.

The middle position the bead proposed is already shipped: tailscale.rs speaks HTTP over /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock and lets tailscaled do the networking. That is the pattern future sources follow.

CONSEQUENCE TO KNOW: the seccomp filter works at socket(2) by family, so it also refuses INBOUND AF_INET. SPEC-HIA:51 names a localhost HTTP gateway at 127.0.0.1:2443 for the browser bridge. It is unimplemented (no reference to 2443 or 127.0.0.1 in any Rust source) and the bridge it was meant for already works -- persona-nmh speaks Native Messaging over stdio in a browser-launched process outside this unit. Building that gateway means revisiting the RestrictAddressFamilies line; the unit and the spec both say so.

macOS has no equivalent enforcement, so there the rule is a convention.
